title: Prefill boundary coalescing and CUDA-graph snapshotting to reduce capture jitter
creator: Miguel Ortega
description:
Problem: Frequent small prefills and misaligned prefill boundaries across concurrent decode streams cause repeated CUDA-graph recaptures and kernel selection divergence. This leads to capture jitter, higher 95/99th latency, and occasional replay failures when KV cache epochs are inconsistent across streams.
Goal: implement a lightweight prefill boundary coalescing layer and a compact CUDA-graph snapshot format that reduces the need for full recapture while preserving correctness for multi-stream decode. We aim to reduce capture incidents by 60% in mixed-batch workloads and eliminate deterministic replay failures seen in stress tests.
Approach: 1) Prefill boundary coalescing: coalesce adjacent prefill windows when their combined sequence length and kernel selection profile match a safe alignment heuristic (sequence_length_delta < 16, identical quantization/profile hints). Add a negotiation phase at request enqueue to adjust batch boundaries conservatively. 2) CUDA-graph snapshotting: capture small, self-contained graph "snapshots" for stable KV epochs (snapshot metadata: epoch_id, kernel_signature, workspace_layout) to allow graph reuse when only KV offset changes. Snapshots are intentionally compact to speed serialization and validation. 3) Epoch fence protocol: introduce a lightweight fence token that orders prefill captures across streams to avoid partial-epoch mixed captures that lead to replay mismatch. 4) Kernel-signature validator: deterministic hash of kernel selection path for a given prefill; on mismatch, fall back to a single-stream decode for safety and log telemetry. 5) Extensive randomized harness and fuzz tests for multi-GPU, preemption, and quantization-mismatch scenarios.
Integration points: runtime capture manager, kernel selector, multi-stream scheduler, and tracing hooks in Console. Success metrics and tests are below.
acceptance_criteria: 95th and 99th tail latency from capture-related stalls reduced by >= 40% on mixed batch benchmark
CUDA-graph recapture events per 10k requests reduced by >= 60% in CI workload
No deterministic replay failures in the randomized multi-stream fuzz harness after 100k runs
Fallback rate (single-stream) is < 0.5% for steady-state traffic
End-to-end correctness validated against golden-decoder for at least 10 representative models (including quantized variants)
test_plan: Unit tests for boundary coalescer heuristics (edge cases: boundary_alignment, size overflow)
Regression tests where KV epoch transitions happen during concurrent prefill
Fuzz harness: spawn 8 streams with random prefill lengths, preemption events, and kernel selection perturbations; assert no mismatch
Perf benchmark: run mixed small/large batches (1-16 tokens prefill) on p4d cluster; measure capture rate and tail latency
Chaos test: simulate GPU preemption and ensure snapshot revalidation and fallback both work without SLO breach
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.prefill_coalesce=true
Canary: enable for 5% of hosted traffic in a single region (us-west-2) for 72 hours
If canary is healthy, increase to 25% for 48 hours and run final regressions
Gradual ramp to 100% over 3 days with telemetry monitoring and automated rollback if capture_failure_rate > 0.1%
Dedicated release note and console dashboard tile for capture metrics and snapshot reuse ratio
risks: Over-aggressive coalescing could increase latency for some user requests if batch waiting is introduced
Kernel signature hashing must be stable across minor allocator/driver changes; otherwise, false mismatches and fallbacks increase
Snapshot serialization/deserialization overhead could negate benefits if not compact
In edge cases, fence protocol may introduce ordering bottlenecks under extreme concurrency
Undiscovered quantization-path divergence might only surface on specific models
notes: Spike results: prototype reduced recapture events by ~48% on small-scale tests (branch: feat/prefill-coalesce-spike)
comments: 2026-02-21 - Miguel Ortega: Kickoff spike completed. Implemented naive coalescer in scheduler and measured preliminary drop in recapture events. Identified a regression when two streams coalesce but choose different kernels because of near-boundary attention length—will add kernel-signature check.
